events.title: Mutiny on the Bounty
events.description: Led by Fletcher Christian, part of the crew of HMS Bounty mutinied against Captain William Bligh in the South Pacific. Bligh and 18 loyalists were set adrift in a launch and navigated nearly 4,000 miles to Timor.
events.significance: One of the most famous mutinies in naval history, it became a lasting subject of books and films and led to the settlement of Pitcairn Island by the mutineers.

events.title: Execution of Benito Mussolini
events.description: Italian dictator Benito Mussolini was captured by Italian partisans while trying to flee to Switzerland and was executed near Lake Como. His body was later displayed in Milan's Piazzale Loreto.
events.significance: His death marked the end of Italian Fascism and came just days before the collapse of Nazi Germany.

events.title: Kon-Tiki Expedition Begins
events.description: Thor Heyerdahl and a crew of five set sail from Callao, Peru, on a balsa raft called Kon-Tiki, aiming to cross the Pacific Ocean to Polynesia. The voyage ended in August 1947 after about 101 days at sea.
events.significance: The expedition supported the idea that pre-Columbian South Americans could have reached Polynesia, and it inspired widespread public interest in archaeology and exploration.

events.title: Birth of Saddam Hussein
events.description: Saddam Hussein, who would become President of Iraq, was born near Tikrit, Iraq. He ruled from 1979 until he was deposed by the 2003 U.S.-led invasion.
events.significance: His rule included the Iran-Iraq War and the Gulf War, shaping Middle Eastern geopolitics for decades.

events.title: First Space Tourist Dennis Tito Launches
events.description: American businessman Dennis Tito launched aboard a Russian Soyuz TM-32 spacecraft and became the first paying space tourist, spending nearly eight days on the International Space Station.
events.significance: His flight opened the door to commercial human spaceflight and private space travel.
